catalog.description: Trained ridge regression - learned from eight seasons of game logs
catalog.summary: A regression trained on eight seasons of real game logs. It learned, from roughly 34,000 past player-games, how much each signal below has actually mattered - nobody hand-picked the weights. Its uncertainty comes from the size of the errors it made on a season it was never trained on, so the probability reflects how wrong this model has genuinely been before.
attends_to: What the opposing defense gives up to the position

catalog.description: Ensemble - parametric shape blended with the player's own history
catalog.summary: Blends two views: a textbook probability curve shaped to fit the stat, and the player's own game-by-game history. With only a few games to go on it leans on the curve, which is smoother; with a long history it leans on what the player has actually done. Weights are not learned - they are set by how much history exists.
attends_to: The player's last 10 games, recent ones weighted more heavily

catalog.summary: Treats yardage the way yardage behaves: never negative, usually clustered low with a long tail of big games, and with a real chance of being held to zero. That lopsided shape is why a player's ceiling sits much further from their typical game than their floor does.
attends_to: How much their yardage swings week to week
How often they get shut out entirely

catalog.summary: For things you count - receptions, carries, touchdowns. You cannot catch 4.3 passes, so this works in whole numbers. It also allows for the fact that usage swings a lot between games, which makes these stats more erratic than a simple counting model would predict.
attends_to: The average number of events per game
How erratic that number is from week to week

catalog.description: Smoothed empirical - the player's games, no assumed shape
catalog.summary: Assumes no shape at all - it just uses the games the player has actually played, smoothed a little so a line falling between two past results still gets a sensible answer. This is the only model that can represent a player who is genuinely feast-or-famine rather than averaging out.
attends_to: Every one of the last 10 games, recent ones weighted more
The actual spread of those results, not an assumed one

catalog.description: Triangular - the original method, evaluated exactly
catalog.summary: The original method, kept for comparison. It draws 10,000 random outcomes from a simple triangle fitted to the best, worst and average of the player's last three games. Because the triangle stops at their best and worst game, it reports 0% for any line beyond that range - which is why it is no longer the default.
